title: You won't fall behind: ThePrimeagen on AI FOMO, burnout and enjoying the moment
summary: ThePrimeagen recounts how fear of falling behind while starting a company at 24 led to 24-hour coding binges and hurt his marriage. He argues the current "you'll be left behind" AI narrative is hype, and that steady daily progress, rest and deep craft beat chasing every new tool.

principles.text: Work hard when it's time to work, but learn to step away; rest doesn't derail your life.
principles.quote: Being engaged and focused and working hard when it's time to work, that is going to pay tons of dividends.

principles.text: One step forward each day is a good day; a weekend off won't change your trajectory.
principles.quote: if every single day you are learning and you're making a step forward, that's a good day. And guess what? On a couple days, if you take a weekend off, that's not going to dramatically change the course of your life.

principles.text: You don't need to keep up with every new tool or model; pick the good work.
principles.quote: So, choose the good things, choose the good work. You don't have to keep up with everything.

principles.text: AI workflows from earlier eras became obsolete, so chasing the latest setup isn't how you stay ahead.
principles.quote: The way you set up context, the way you use it, the way you interact with it today, looks almost nothing like it did in the beginning.

principles.text: Understand the underlying thing instead of relying on a lucky-button shortcut; that is what pays off.
principles.quote: Learning and actually understanding the underlying thing instead of pressing the I'm going to be lucky tonight button, yeah, that's going to pay off a lot of dividends.

principles.text: Be skeptical of vendors pushing you to burn tokens, but stay curious and form an informed opinion without betting everything.
principles.quote: Don't you realize that there's a little bit of a perverse incentive when the people who are selling shovels telling you the only thing you ever need to practice or do is dig holes?
